messages:
alex: Proposal — 'saturation safety-net' for runtime. Goal: keep p99 under 80ms for interactive SLO while avoiding catastrophic throughput collapse when GPU hits saturation. Hybrid approach: kernel downgrade -> microbatch shrink -> selective shedding. Short thread, quick feedback?

maria: sketch the state machine pls. do we prefer kernel switches over batch changes? any cost math? :thinking_face:

alex: state machine (high-level):
1) monitor p99 and GPU util windowed (10s).
2) if p99 > SLO && util > 88% -> try kernel downgrade (same model variant, quantized/fast kernel) if seq_len <= kernel_max_seq.
3) if kernel downgrade not applicable or p99 still > SLO after X ms -> shrink microbatch size by 50% (min 1).
4) if still violating -> shed low-priority traffic (embeddings, bulk rerank) via token-aware admission.

Pseudoconfig we can test:
```json
{"safety_net": {"p99_slo_ms": 80, "util_threshold": 0.88, "kernel_downgrade": {"enabled": true, "allowed_kernels": ["fast-fp16-q4", "int8-fused"]}, "microbatch": {"shrink_factor": 0.5, "min_batch": 1}, "shed_order": ["bulk-embedding", "low-qps-batch"]}}
```

jun: kv cache question — switching kernels will change kv-layout/quantization. do we blow the cache on switch? that's expensive for warm chat sessions.

alex: good point. plan: maintain per-kernel-tag KV caches keyed by (model, kernel_tag). fallback path reads from primary cache; if miss, we asynchronously warm alternate cache while serving from primary. cost numbers from last perf run: warming full chat history (2k tokens) ~120ms extra per cold session, but amortized over long sessions.

perf-runner: loadtest snapshot (staging, 1k RPS mixed):
- median token latency: 5.9ms
- p95 token latency: 21.8ms
- p99 token latency: 72.4ms
- GPU util (windowed 30s): 94.1%
- observed kernel_switches/sec: 0.0 (no safety net enabled)
- kv_miss_rate: 2.3%
- throughput (tokens/sec): 8.2M
logs: "p99 jumps when util > 90% and batch > 8"

sophie: shrinking microbatch reduces p99 but costs throughput. rough back-of-envelope from the same experiment: 18% drop in tokens/sec when batch cap reduced from 8->4. we need to quantify cost per unit latency win.

maria: can we do partial batching (mix small interactive batches and large non-interactive) to preserve throughput? also prefer shedding non-critical queues before microbatch shrink?

alex: idea: admission policies can be per-route. interactive routes get kernel downgrade first; background jobs get batch shrink then shed. ordering can be route-configurable.

jun: on KV dual-cache: impl effort ~2-3 days + tests. memory overhead ~ +12% per model per kernel-tag. need SRE buy-in for mem bump.

perf-runner: quick A/B simulation results (model x, seq<=512):
AB test: control (no safety net) vs safety_net_v0.1 (kernel downgrade + batch shrink + shedding).
- control p99: 72ms -> safety_net p99: 54ms
- control tokens/sec: 8.2M -> safety_net: 6.9M (16% drop)
- shed_count (per min): 0 -> 120 (mostly bulk embeddings)
- kernel_switch_rate: 9/min during bursts
- cost delta (estimated infra): +3.2% due to shedding inefficiency + cache warmups

maria: tradeoffs look plausible. we need thresholds: when to prefer shedding vs throughput loss. propose metrics to monitor during canary: [p50,p95,p99,gpu_util,reqs_shed,kernel_switch_rate,kv_miss_rate,cost_per_token].

alex: canary plan: roll safety_net_v0.1 on staging for 30m, synthetic burst replay at 1k RPS then 3min spike to 1.6k, observe. If p99 reduces to <80ms and shed_rate < 300/min and cost delta <5% -> promote to prod canary (low-ramp).

sophie: simulate throughput loss impact on tail SLA (p99 for business-critical routes). I'll run microbench to measure tail under mixed batching. assign to me.

jun: I'll prototype dual-kv-cache and a lightweight kernel_tag switch API. aiming for branch PR by EOD.

perf-runner: scheduling loadtest now, will post results under this thread when done.

infra-bot: Reminder: starting staging canary job #8765 in 10m — watch /metrics/canary/safety_net_v0.1.

maria: ok let's keep initial canary short. if we see too many sheath events or cache thrash, abort. :thumbsup:

alex: tl;dr — hybrid safety net (kernel->batch->shed) + per-kernel kv caches + per-route policy. action items: @jun prototype, @sophie microbench throughput sim, @perf-runner run A/B and post logs, @maria monitor metrics and abort criteria.

maria: thanks. tagging infra on standby.

alex: updating RFC doc with state machine + config example, will ping when ready. :rocket:
